Interface CausalAudit

public interface CausalAudit
Receives Parsley's per-record causal-buffering events: forwarded, held, released, evicted (causal violation), eviction-limit-exceeded (fail-fast instead of a violation), undecodable, and unresolvable-clock (an undecodable dependencies header at ingest). Register one with CausalProcessors.Builder.withAudit(CausalAudit) to route these events wherever your audit/compliance trail needs them (a SIEM, a durable audit store, structured logs) — Parsley itself never decides where they go.

Every method here carries record identity and causal metadata only — topic, partition, offset, and the causal gap — never the record's key or value. Parsley's logs follow the same rule; this interface exists for callers who need that information delivered somewhere durable and queryable rather than (or in addition to) a text log line.

This is a separate, independent concern from ParsleyMetrics: metrics are Parsley-internal aggregate counters wired automatically into the Kafka Streams metrics registry, while a CausalAudit is optional, client-supplied, and carries per-record identity. Both are notified of the same underlying events; neither depends on the other.

Failure handling: an exception thrown from any method here is caught and logged by Parsley — it never fails the record or the Streams task. A slow implementation will, however, add latency to the calling thread, since these methods are called synchronously from the processing path; keep implementations fast and non-blocking (hand off to a queue if the destination is slow).

Thread-safety: one instance is shared across every task/partition the processor runs on, each owned by its own Kafka Streams thread. Implementations must be thread-safe.

    • recordHeld

      void recordHeld(String topic, int partition, long offset, int bufferDepth, CausalDependencies gap)
      A record's causal dependencies were not yet satisfied; it was admitted to the buffer to wait.
      Parameters:
      topic - the record's source topic
      partition - the record's source partition
      offset - the record's source offset
      bufferDepth - the buffer's depth after admitting this record
      gap - the dependencies not yet satisfied by the frontier

    • recordReleased

      void recordReleased(String topic, int partition, long offset, int bufferDepthAfter)
      A previously held record became causally satisfiable and was released from the buffer, in causal order.
      Parameters:
      topic - the record's source topic
      partition - the record's source partition
      offset - the record's source offset
      bufferDepthAfter - the buffer's depth after releasing this record

    • recordViolation

      void recordViolation(String topic, int partition, long offset, CausalDependencies gap)
      A held record was evicted and forwarded out of causal order because a CausalBufferLimit fired before its dependencies were satisfied — a causal violation.
      Parameters:
      topic - the record's source topic
      partition - the record's source partition
      offset - the record's source offset
      gap - the dependencies that remained unsatisfied at the time of eviction

    • recordDeserializationFailure

      void recordDeserializationFailure(String topic, int partition, long offset, String reason, boolean dropped)
      A held record could no longer be deserialised on the forward path (e.g. an incompatible Schema Registry change while buffered).
      Parameters:
      topic - the record's source topic
      partition - the record's source partition
      offset - the record's source offset
      reason - an operator-facing diagnostic (coordinate, dependencies, lengths, schema id — never the payload bytes)
      dropped - true if the record was dropped and processing continued (parsley.buffer.deserialization.failure.policy = continue); false if it remains in the buffer for recovery (the fail default)

    • recordClockResolutionFailure

      void recordClockResolutionFailure(String topic, int partition, long offset, String reason, boolean failed)
      An inbound record's parsley-causal-dependencies header could not be decoded into a clock (a corrupt or truncated header, or one in an unsupported wire version).
      Parameters:
      topic - the record's source topic
      partition - the record's source partition
      offset - the record's source offset
      reason - an operator-facing diagnostic (coordinate, encoded header length — never the payload bytes)
      failed - true if the task is being failed fast (the fail default of parsley.clock.resolution.failure.policy); false if the record was forwarded with empty dependencies (continue)

    • recordEvictionLimitExceeded

      void recordEvictionLimitExceeded(String topic, int partition, long offset, CausalDependencies gap)
      A CausalBufferLimit fired on a held record whose dependencies were not yet satisfied, and parsley.buffer.eviction.failure.policy = fail (the default) is configured: the record was not evicted — it remains buffered — and the owning Streams task is about to fail fast rather than deliver it out of causal order.
      Parameters:
      topic - the record's source topic
      partition - the record's source partition
      offset - the record's source offset
      gap - the dependencies that remain unsatisfied
